title: Color Study — guide catalog
description: Editable text and extracted artwork for all 20 approved glossary and practical guide screens.
asset_id_policy: IDs are stable local catalog identifiers, not provider or Library IDs. Illustrations had no separate file IDs in the source PNGs; each is now an extracted PNG with source provenance.
text_policy: Manually transcribed guide text; line wraps normalized. Supplementary full-screen OCR is unverified and is not the canonical guide copy.
coordinate_system: crop_xyxy is [left, top, right, bottom], pixels from source top-left; right and bottom are exclusive.

ui.no_results: No matching guides. Try another term.

guides.title: Understand your color
guides.description: Key concepts to help you explore, compare and communicate color with confidence.

entries.title: Hue
entries.description: The color family, such as red, yellow or blue.

entries.title: Value
entries.description: How light or dark a color is.

entries.title: Chroma
entries.description: Distance from neutral gray at the same value.

entries.title: Temperature
entries.description: How warm or cool a color feels relative to another.

guides.tip: Try it: lock hue, then explore value and chroma.

guides.title: Build a color harmony

entries.title: Analogous
entries.description: Neighboring hues on the color wheel.

entries.title: Complementary
entries.description: Opposing hues on a chosen color wheel.

entries.title: Split-complementary
entries.description: One hue plus the two hues beside its complement.

entries.title: Neutralize
entries.description: Reduce chroma toward a neutral gray.

guides.tip: Paint mixing complements can differ from visual complements.

guides.title: See color in context
guides.description: Our eyes and brains don’t see colors in isolation. Learn how context, light, and display limits can change what you see.

entries.title: Simultaneous contrast
entries.description: Surrounding colors change how a color appears.
entries.additional_description: The same color can look lighter or darker depending on what’s around it.

entries.title: Value structure
entries.description: The arrangement of light and dark shapes.
entries.additional_description: Differences in value (lightness and darkness) create contrast, hierarchy, and clarity — even without color.

entries.title: Gamut
entries.description: The range of colors a palette or display can produce.
entries.additional_description: Different materials and devices can show different ranges of color. A wider gamut can display more vivid and saturated colors.

guides.tip: Compare the same focal color on different backgrounds.
guides.header_description: Short, practical explanations to help you understand color and make better decisions.
guides.tip_description: See how context changes what you perceive, and try it yourself in the Context view.

guides.title: Understand paint behavior
guides.description: Learn how paint changes a color, and what to expect in real materials.

entries.title: Tint
entries.description: A color mixed with white.

entries.title: Shade
entries.description: A color mixed with black.

entries.title: Glaze
entries.description: A thin transparent color layer over dry paint.

entries.title: Scumble
entries.description: A thin, broken layer of relatively opaque paint.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.description: How fully paint hides the layer beneath.

entries.title: Undertone
entries.description: The color revealed in a thin application.

guides.tip: Digital previews suggest effects; real pigments behave differently.

guides.title: Color language

entries.title: Saturation
entries.description: Often used like chroma in studios; technically a different measure.

entries.title: Intensity
entries.description: Studio shorthand for how strong or vivid a color appears.

entries.title: Brightness
entries.description: May mean lightness or vividness. Specify which you mean.

entries.title: Tone
entries.description: Can mean value, overall color character, or a gray mixture.

entries.title: Achromatic
entries.description: Without hue: neutral black, white and gray.

entries.title: Chromatic gray
entries.description: A low-chroma gray with a discernible hue.

guides.tip: Ask: should this be lighter, more vivid, or warmer?

guides.title: Mixing with intention

entries.title: Tint
entries.description: A color mixed with white; hue and chroma may also change.

entries.title: Shade
entries.description: A color mixed with black; the hue may also shift.

entries.title: Neutralize
entries.description: Reduce chroma using a suitable mixing color.

entries.title: Mixing complement
entries.description: A paint that mixes with another to produce a neutral.

entries.title: Chromatic black
entries.description: A very dark mixture made from colored pigments.

entries.title: Subtractive mixing
entries.description: Pigments absorb parts of the light; mixtures depend on the pigments.

guides.tip: Adjust value, hue and chroma, then recheck the mixture in context.

guides.title: Design your palette
guides.description: Key concepts to help you plan and build a purposeful color palette.

entries.title: Limited palette
entries.description: A deliberately small selection of paints.

entries.title: Split-primary palette
entries.description: Two versions of each traditional primary for different mixing directions.

entries.title: Color string
entries.description: Premixed steps through value, hue or chroma.

entries.title: Mother color
entries.description: A shared color added to mixtures to help unify them.

entries.title: Gamut mapping
entries.description: Fit observed colors into your available range while preserving relationships.

entries.title: Earth colors
entries.description: Ochres, siennas, umbers and related natural or synthetic colors.

guides.tip: No three actual paints can mix every visible color.

guides.title: Read light on form

entries.title: Local color
entries.description: An object’s characteristic color, apart from lighting effects.

entries.title: Observed color
entries.description: The color perceived under the current light and surroundings.

entries.title: Light family
entries.description: Planes receiving direct illumination from the main light.

entries.title: Halftone
entries.description: A turning plane within the light family.

entries.title: Terminator
entries.description: The boundary where a surface turns away from direct light.

entries.title: Form shadow
entries.description: Shadow on a surface facing away from the light.

guides.tip: First separate the light family from the shadow family.

guides.title: Understand shadows and reflections
guides.description: Key concepts to help you explore, compare and communicate color with confidence.

entries.title: Core shadow
entries.description: A darker region within a form shadow, when present.

entries.title: Cast shadow
entries.description: A shadow projected onto another surface by an obstruction.

entries.title: Contact shadow
entries.description: A dark region where little surrounding light reaches a contact.

entries.title: Reflected light
entries.description: Light bounced onto a surface from nearby objects.

entries.title: Highlight
entries.description: A reflection of the light source, shaped by material and viewpoint.

entries.title: Temperature shift
entries.description: A change toward a warmer or cooler color relative to another.

guides.tip: Warm light and cool shadows are a possibility, not a universal rule.

guides.title: Compose with color

entries.title: Dominant color
entries.description: The color family that sets the prevailing impression.

entries.title: Accent color
entries.description: A limited color used to attract attention or create contrast.

entries.title: High-key / low-key
entries.description: A mainly light or mainly dark value arrangement.

entries.title: Notan
entries.description: A design of light and dark masses, often reduced to two values.

entries.title: Value compression
entries.description: Reduce the observed light-dark range to fit the painting.

entries.title: Chroma hierarchy
entries.description: Distribute stronger and weaker chroma to establish emphasis.

guides.tip: A focal point can rely on value contrast, edges or placement as well as chroma.

guides.title: Perception and atmosphere

entries.title: Chromatic adaptation
entries.description: Vision adjusts to the prevailing illumination.

entries.title: Color constancy
entries.description: Objects can seem similar in color even as lighting changes.

entries.title: Afterimage
entries.description: A residual visual response after looking away from a color.

entries.title: Optical mixing
entries.description: Separate small marks visually combine at a viewing distance.

entries.title: Broken color
entries.description: Distinct touches remain partly separate to retain color variation.

entries.title: Aerial perspective
entries.description: Distance through atmosphere changes contrast and color.

guides.tip: Try it: judge a passage beside its neighbors and at the intended viewing distance.

guides.title: Know your paint

entries.title: Pigment
entries.description: The coloring particles in paint.

entries.title: Binder
entries.description: The material holding pigment; oil paint uses a drying oil.

entries.title: Medium
entries.description: An addition that changes handling and may affect gloss or transparency.

entries.title: Masstone
entries.description: A paint’s appearance in a substantial, concentrated application.

entries.title: Tinting strength
entries.description: How strongly a pigment influences a mixture.

entries.title: Color Index
entries.description: A pigment identifier, such as PB29, more specific than a marketing name.

guides.tip: Transparency and tinting strength are different properties.

guides.title: Layers and surface
guides.description: Key concepts to help you explore, compare and communicate color with confidence.

entries.title: Imprimatura
entries.description: An initial thin tone applied to the ground.

entries.title: Underpainting
entries.description: An initial painted structure beneath later layers.

entries.title: Grisaille
entries.description: Monochromatic painting, usually gray, often used beneath color.

entries.title: Alla prima
entries.description: Direct painting completed while the paint remains wet.

entries.title: Impasto
entries.description: Thick paint whose texture catches light and casts small shadows.

entries.title: Sinking in
entries.description: Paint dries matte or dull, changing its apparent richness.

guides.tip: Layer thickness, the ground and surface gloss all affect perceived color.

guides.title: Decode studio feedback

entries.title: Muddy
entries.description: Color or value relationships are less clear than intended.

entries.title: Chalky
entries.description: Light passages feel pale, opaque or disconnected from the lighting.

entries.title: Too hot
entries.description: May mean too warm, too vivid or too visually dominant.

entries.title: Luminous
entries.description: Color relationships create an impression of light or glow.

entries.title: Lightfast
entries.description: Resistant to light-induced color change.

entries.title: Fugitive
entries.description: Prone to fading or other color change under light.

guides.tip: Try it: translate vague critique into a specific value, hue, chroma or surface adjustment.

guides.title: Color troubleshooting

entries.title: Too pale
entries.description: Check value first. Lower it if needed, then reassess chroma.

entries.title: Too vivid
entries.description: Reduce chroma while keeping the intended value.

entries.title: Too dark
entries.description: Raise value, then recheck hue and chroma.

entries.title: Too warm
entries.description: Shift hue toward a cooler comparison color.

entries.title: Muddy
entries.description: Check value separation and hue relationships before adding chroma.

entries.title: Wrong on canvas
entries.description: Judge the color beside its neighbors and on the intended background.

guides.tip: Change one control at a time, then compare with the original.

guides.title: Choosing axes and locks

entries.title: Choose two axes
entries.description: Map two dimensions to the field, such as value and chroma.

entries.title: Hold a dimension
entries.description: Lock a control to keep it fixed while exploring others.

entries.title: Hue × Value
entries.description: Explore color families and lightness at a selected chroma.

entries.title: Value × Chroma
entries.description: Explore lightness and intensity while holding hue.

entries.title: Relative warmth
entries.description: Warmth often changes hue; a hue lock can conflict with this adjustment.

entries.title: Gamut boundary
entries.description: Some combinations cannot be displayed. Keep unavailable regions marked.

guides.tip: Use value and chroma as your first axes; select a hue to hold fixed.

guides.title: Harmony recipes

entries.title: Monochromatic
entries.description: One hue varied through value and chroma.

entries.title: Analogous
entries.description: Neighboring hues for continuity and gentle variation.

entries.title: Complementary
entries.description: Opposing hues on a chosen wheel for strong contrast.

entries.title: Split-complementary
entries.description: One hue plus the two hues beside its complement.

entries.title: Triadic
entries.description: Three hues spaced approximately evenly around the wheel.

entries.title: Tetradic
entries.description: Two complementary pairs; choose a dominant hue to organize them.

guides.tip: Vary area, value and chroma. A harmony does not require equal amounts.

guides.title: Edges and emphasis

entries.title: Hard edge
entries.description: An abrupt transition that can sharpen a boundary.

entries.title: Soft edge
entries.description: A gradual transition that can suggest turning form or atmosphere.

entries.title: Lost edge
entries.description: A boundary that merges with its surroundings.

entries.title: Found edge
entries.description: A boundary that becomes distinct again after a lost passage.

entries.title: Focal contrast
entries.description: Local differences in value or color can attract attention.

entries.title: Edge hierarchy
entries.description: Vary edge sharpness to organize attention across the painting.

guides.tip: Reserve strong contrasts and sharp edges where they serve your focus.

guides.title: Screen versus paint

entries.title: Additive color
entries.description: Screens combine emitted red, green and blue light.

entries.title: Subtractive color
entries.description: Pigments absorb and scatter light; physical mixtures depend on the paints.

entries.title: Hex value
entries.description: A digital RGB specification, not a pigment mixing recipe.

entries.title: Display gamut
entries.description: The range of colors a screen can reproduce.

entries.title: Viewing light
entries.description: Illumination changes how physical paint appears.

entries.title: Surface effects
entries.description: Gloss, texture and layer thickness affect painted color.

guides.tip: Use screen previews to explore relationships; verify mixtures with real paint.

guides.title: Common misconceptions

entries.title: Warm light, cool shadows?
entries.description: Sometimes. Shadow color depends on ambient and reflected light.

entries.title: Never use black?
entries.description: Black is a useful pigment. Judge its effect on your mixture.

entries.title: Gray means muddy?
entries.description: Grays can be clear and expressive; context determines their role.

entries.title: White only lightens?
entries.description: White can also change hue, chroma and opacity.

entries.title: Warm colors always advance?
entries.description: Edges, value contrast and spatial cues can outweigh temperature.

entries.title: Complements always make gray?
entries.description: Actual pigment pairs and proportions determine the mixture.

guides.tip: Treat painting rules as starting points. Observe the specific relationship.
